simple.meaning: שִׁלּוּחַ (shillûwach) is a Hebrew word meaning “(only in plural) a dismissal , i.e. (of a wife) divorce (especially the document); also (of a daughter) dower.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שִׁלּוּחַ (H7964) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 18:2, with occurrences in Exodus, 1 Kings, Micah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שִׁלּוּחַ (H7964) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שִׁלּוּחַ (H7964) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שִׁלּוּחַ (shillûwach) / H7964 is traced through Exodus 18:2, 1 Kings 9:16, Micah 1:14 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: (only in plural) a dismissal , i.e. (of a wife) divorce (especially the document); also (of a daughter) dower
definitions.full: H7964. shilluchim שִׁלּוּחִים noun [masculine] plural sending away, parting gift ; — 1 שִׁלוּחֶיהָ אַחר Exod 18:2 (J) after she had been sent away. 2 שִׁלֻּחִים 1Kin 9:16 he gave (city) as parting gift (i.e. dowry) to his daughter; compare figurative שִׁלּוּחִים Micah 1:14 thou shalt give a pearting gift (= say farewell to, lose) Morešeth of Gath.

occurrences.englishText: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, received Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after he had sent her away,
Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, taken Gezer, burned it with fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it for a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
Therefore you will give a parting gift to Moresheth Gath.
